instructions: Cut the 8 oz kefalograviera into 4 slices about 1/2 inch thick. Any thinner and they melt before the outside browns.
Put a shallow bowl of cold water next to the stove. Spread the 1/3 cup flour on a plate and stir in the pinch of pepper.
Dip a slice of cheese in the water and let it drip for a second. Press both sides and the edges into the flour, then shake off the extra. Coat the rest the same way.
Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in a large nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Lay in the slices with room between them.
Leave them alone for 1 to 2 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and crisp. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. If they brown too fast, turn the heat down to medium.
Flip them carefully with a thin spatula and cook the other side for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's golden and the middle feels soft when you press it.
Transfer them to a plate. Cut the lemon into wedges and squeeze 2 of them over the hot cheese.
Serve right away with the rest of the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three versions coat 1/2 inch slices of a firm Greek cheese in flour and fry them in a little olive oil for a minute or two a side, then squeeze lemon over the top. The Daring Gourmet (the lead) rinses the slices so the flour sticks and lets you use semolina or plain flour; Eating European and Tara's Multicultural Table dip the cheese in water first, and both use kefalograviera, which is what this one uses. The flaming brandy or ouzo that restaurants add is left out, as most versions treat it as optional. No version read had 20 or more ratings (the lead has 7 votes, Eating European 5), and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for this cuisine, has no fried cheese saganaki, so the lead is the strongest version read.
